BIO215 model comparison plan — fixed before fitting, 2026-10-19 (Beijing)

Data: Kaggle / UCI Wisconsin Diagnostic, 569 observations, 30 numeric predictors.
Keep the existing seed-123 split: training 454 (285 B, 169 M), test 115 (72 B, 43 M).
The test set was already examined during feasibility work. It is a fixed internal
hold-out audit, not an untouched external validation cohort. Do not change it.

On training observations only, create shared stratified five-fold partitions for
three repeats with seeds 2151, 2152 and 2153. Each observation is validation once
per repeat. Fit preprocessing using each fold's fitting observations only.
Candidates: random forest (500 trees, mtry=5, all 30 features); random forest
(500 trees, mtry=3, 10 mean features); ridge logistic regression (alpha=0,
lambda=0.01,0.1,1, all 30 features); ridge logistic regression (lambda=0.1,
10 mean features); radial SVM (cost=0.5,2,8; gamma=1/30, all 30 features).
glmnet and SVM standardization is learned inside each training fold. No ID or
diagnosis enters predictors. No additional feature selection uses test labels.
The prespecified 30-versus-10 comparison tests feature reduction without using
the complete dataset to rank features. Report unsuccessful reductions too.

Select the candidate with highest mean validation AUROC across the 15 folds.
Exact ties: fewer active features, then candidate order above. These CV scores
are used for selection, not claimed to be an unbiased final performance estimate.
Refit once on all 454 training observations using seed 21500. Audit the selected
model once on the unchanged 115 test observations; do not change the winner,
threshold, features, or hyperparameters in response. Threshold P(M)>=0.5.
Retain historical feasibility outputs. Retain all fold assignments, predictions,
configuration, metrics and timing. Report ROC/PR curves, accuracy, sensitivity,
specificity, F1, AUROC, AUPRC, Brier score and calibration. Bootstrap the fixed
test predictions for descriptive 95% uncertainty intervals, not external claims.

Interpretation after selection: held-out permutation importance (AUROC decrease)
and model-agnostic Monte Carlo SHAP for P(M), training-only background. SHAP
is approximate, adjusted for local additivity, with fixed seed and at least 128
simulations. Assess stability against an independent higher-simulation run on a
small prespecified subset. Correlated nuclear size features limit attribution;
SHAP is a model explanation, not causal evidence or clinical validation.

Shiny and the BIO215 R package must use byte-identical model objects and shared
prediction/validation source. Package default output must be predicted classes.
Verify installation, R CMD check, examples, malformed inputs, reordered columns,
and identity of all 115 package versus Shiny predictions. Retain test logs.
Prepare GitHub-ready source and README.Rmd; public publication is a separate step.

Design: original pink palette inspired by the breast cancer awareness ribbon;
no charity logo or affiliation. Use dark text and buttons; verify text contrast,
keyboard navigation, narrow screens and every existing prediction/data workflow.

Sources: https://breastcancernow.org/get-involved/breast-cancer-awareness-month
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html
https://glmnet.stanford.edu/articles/glmnet.html
https://bgreenwell.github.io/fastshap/reference/explain.html
https://doi.org/10.24432/C5DW2B

Implementation note after selecting the ridge model: also provide exact linear
interventional SHAP on log-odds for immediate Shiny/package explanations. This
does not replace the planned probability-scale Monte Carlo SHAP audit. Formula
and assumptions follow https://shap.readthedocs.io/en/latest/generated/shap.LinearExplainer.html .
fastshap current CRAN installation was unavailable; use CRAN archive version 0.1.1.
